text:
emma.cs: we have multiple customers reporting p95/p99 latency spikes since the overnight maintenance window. starts ~2026-03-14 22:00 UTC. lots of generation endpoints hitting 1.8-2.5s p99 vs normal ~250-400ms. escalated from support.

mike-sre: saw alerts for batcher queue length +500 on Dedicated pool 'eu-west-1-gpu-a' around 22:15. rolling averages show tail latency jump correlated with driver/vm kernel updates pushed in the window.

liang-runtime: confirming — across several hosts we see GPU-side stalls reported in runtime logs: "gpu stall: waiting for pagefault completion" and prolonged key-value cache flushes. sample from runtime logs:
`````
[2026-03-14T22:16:02Z] batcher: queue_size=523 p50=120ms p95=980ms p99=2100ms
[2026-03-14T22:16:14Z] device(2): stall_detected reason=host_io_wait duration_ms=1850
`````

sophia-infra: infra change notes: kernel 6.4.12 + Nvidia driver 535.103 pushed at 21:45, also firmware microcode update to GPU FW v1.4.7 on the same hosts.

emma.cs: customers included two mid-market teams and one AI startup. repro steps from one customer:
`````
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","prompt":"x"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -w "time_total:%{time_total}\n"
# returns time_total ~2.1s for multiple runs
`````

mike-sre: quick diagnostics pushed:
- iostat -x 1 3 shows avg await on /dev/nvme0n1 spikes to 25-40ms during the window
- dmesg tails show repeated 'nvme: completion timeout' messages on some hosts
- top/ps show kworker threads high CPU

liang-runtime: also saw slew of PCIe AER errors in kern.log on 3 hosts, then runtime started serializing requests to avoid corruption. stack traces point at new driver behaving badly under IO pressure.

incident-bot: runbook check: this looks like a hardware+driver+host-io interaction. recommended triage steps: 1) isolate traffic to a single host 2) repro under controlled load 3) attempt rollback of driver 4) throttle background IO

emma.cs: immediate mitigation requested from infra — can we roll back drivers on one pool and see effect? customers are very unhappy.

sophia-infra: rolling back driver on pool eu-west-1-gpu-a now to 525.xx (previous stable). will cordon hosts and apply.

deploy-bot: cordon initiated for hosts: gpu-a-1,gpu-a-2,gpu-a-3

mike-sre: also paused background snapshot jobs and increased cgroup io.latency target for model cache writes.

--- 22:40 UTC ---

sophia-infra: rollback complete on gpu-a hosts, restarting runtime pods.

liang-runtime: after rollback, quick measurements show p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~340ms on the rolled pool for same test prompt. batcher queue length normalized.

emma.cs: customers on the rolled pool confirm perceived latency reduced. putting note to CS to route traffic there temporarily.

mike-sre: left a probe running across other pools — some still show elevated p99 (1.2s), likely hosts still on new driver/fw or still had hit with IO backlog.

sophia-infra: chasing hosts with persistent nvme timeouts; we suspect a firmware regression that interacts poorly with driver 535 under certain IO patterns. opened ticket with hw vendor and Nvidia.

liang-runtime: action items:
- short: pin affected Dedicated pools to driver 525 until vendor fix (DONE on eu-west-1-gpu-a)
- short: throttle snapshot/io jobs and move them to maintenance windows
- med: add runtime watchdog to detect sustained device stalls and fast-fail to fallback model variant
- med: add telemetry to correlate nvme await / pci errors with batcher queue length
- long: bisect across kernel, driver, fw combos on a repro rack; prepare microbench harness (fio + synthetic generation load) to find the smallest repro.

emma.cs: also flagged billing/SLAs — will need to credit affected tenants if p99 > SLA for the window.

mike-sre: for immediate customer comms: message sent to affected tenants describing mitigation (rolled back driver on subset, ongoing investigation, ticket opened with vendor). :white_check_mark:

sophia-infra: note for postmortem: don't push kernel+gpu driver+firmware in the same maintenance window. add an integration test that runs fio + synthetic model run on a canary host after upgrades.

liang-runtime: I'm collecting logs and will attach a concise artifact: sample kernel logs, nvidia-smi dmon during the event, runtime metrics, and fio traces. will drop in the incident board.

emma.cs: thanks all — keeping this thread open until vendor response and full rollback plan done. follow-ups: @sophia-infra own rollback plan for remaining pools; @liang-runtime own repro harness and telemetry; @mike-sre coordinate customer credits and comms.

incident-bot: severity: Sev3 -> Escalated to engineering triage. Incident owner: sophia-infra. Timeline note created.

mike-sre: rough timeline for follow-ups: bisect next 48-72h, vendor reply expected 72h, temporary pin for 2 weeks.

emma.cs: closing loop with customers now. will update as we hear back. :pray:
